page: Amazon Web Services t3.small is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512, AES, and BMI2. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, equivalent to 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no local storage, requiring network-attached storage options, and contains 0 GPUs.

Benchmark results place the computational and memory subsystem in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems. Under stress-ng, it delivers a single-core score of 935.99 and a multi-core score of 1364.45. Memory bandwidth reaches 70.12 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached reads, falling to 8.1 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 8.82 GB/sec for uncached writes. Overall processing capacity reflects low compute density, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 1893.8 and a PassMark memory score of 807.58. Microbenchmarks register gzip compression at 15.04 GB/sec, bzip3 decompression at 4.56 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput at 1.64 million operations per second.

The t3.small relies on a burstable CPU credit allocation model, making it a cost-efficient option for entry-level tasks rather than sustained execution. With a 0 Gbps baseline network rating and the absence of attached local drives, continuous heavy workloads encounter performance throttling. The configuration is primarily tailored for lightweight utility tasks, development environments, low-traffic web serving, microservices, and small background cron jobs.
